name: refactor_python_dict_dispatch
description: Refactors a long if/elif command chain into a dict dispatch table without changing behavior
prompts: handle(command, value) in router.py applies a named command to value via a long if/elif chain: 'inc' adds 1, 'dec' subtracts 1, 'double' multiplies by 2, 'square' raises to the power 2, and any unknown command returns value unchanged. Refactor it to use a dictionary dispatch table (map each command name to a function/lambda) instead of the if/elif chain, so adding commands is data-driven. Do not change observable behavior: the four commands compute the same results and an unknown command still returns value unchanged. Keep the handle(command, value) signature.

test_setup_files.test_router.py:
from router import handle


def test_known_commands():
    assert handle("inc", 5) == 6
    assert handle("dec", 5) == 4
    assert handle("double", 5) == 10
    assert handle("square", 5) == 25


def test_unknown_returns_unchanged():
    assert handle("nope", 5) == 5
    assert handle("", 0) == 0
